nodes.description: Immutable address storing the deployer/owner; used as access-control principal and recipient of withdrawn funds.
Immutable IERC20 reference to the hardcoded WETH address; unused in logic but part of contract state.
Constant uint256 value of 1000000000 ether; deceptive name, never used in any code path.
Immutable address constant hardcoded to 0xFd49...ba19; never referenced in any function.
Bait constructor; assigns msg.sender to the immutable owner slot me.
Payable receive fallback that accepts ether with empty body; holds the contract balance.
External function that requires msg.sender == me and then forwards the full contract balance to me via a low-level call.
External function taking an attacker-supplied address and delegatecalling finesse() on it, giving arbitrary code/storage control.
Caller of the constructor, used to initialize the immutable owner me; trust anchor of the contract.
Caller of withdraw; compared against me in the access-control require.
Low-level delegatecall to the user-supplied _pickpocket address encoding finesse(); executes arbitrary code in this contract's storage context.
Low-level call{value: address(this).balance} to me inside withdraw; external value transfer with no reentrancy guard.
External address parameter of bait(); the arbitrary delegatecall target supplied by the caller.
Local bool capturing the success flag of the low-level call in withdraw.
Local bool capturing the success flag of the delegatecall in bait.

edges.reason: msg.sender flows into the constructor, which permanently fixes the access-control principal me.
constructor writes msg.sender into the immutable state variable me, establishing ownership.
msg.sender is read in withdraw to enforce require(msg.sender == me), the only privilege check in the contract.
withdraw reads the immutable me as the comparison target of its access-control require.
withdraw triggers an external value transfer of the whole balance to me without a reentrancy guard or effects-first ordering.
me is used as the recipient of the low-level call inside withdraw.
bait unconditionally executes a delegatecall, letting any caller run arbitrary code in the contract's storage context.
The attacker-controlled _pickpocket parameter is used directly as the delegatecall target, so the callee is fully user-controlled.
_pickpocket is the input parameter consumed by bait.
The success flag returned by the low-level call is stored in the local variable checked by require(success).
The success flag returned by the delegatecall is stored in the local variable checked by require(success).

normalization_plan.reason: The parameter _pickpocket only exists to feed the delegatecall inside bait; it has no independent identity and should be folded into the bait function node.
The local bool success in withdraw merely holds the return flag of the low-level call and is only used by the immediate require, so it folds into the call@withdraw unsafe operation.
The local bool success in bait merely holds the delegatecall return flag used by the immediate require, so it folds into the delegatecall@bait unsafe operation.
